thread:
incident-bot: 🔔 ALERT: hosted-api-us-east - request_queue_depth > 10k for 3m, p95 latency 2.8s, p99 6.1s. Trigger: queue-growth-autoscale. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/teams/hosted-api/d/queue

oncall-jordan: I’m on it. Paging SRE. first-pass: confirm scope and customers impacted.

maya: seeing same on traces. lots of small gen requests holding KV cache, also many long-context jobs.

sina: fwiw autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempt but backoff: "ScaleRequestRejected: gpu_quota_exceeded" starting ~2136451000.

aj: that matches cloud quota spikes - looks like we exhausted ephemeral GPU quota in us-east zone.

oncall-jordan: timeline: traffic surge began ~2136450500, backlog growth sharp after 2136450800. Autoscaler tried to create pods but failed due to quota. We need mitigation steps: 1) reduce incoming QPS for heavy tenants, 2) enable model fallback routing to smaller quantized variant, 3) borrow capacity from dedicated pool / region.

ken: I'm on dedicated pool ops - can we temporarily allow hosted requests into dedicated-us-east-2 pool? that'll need quick ACL flip.

maya: to reduce blast radius I can push per-tenant RBAC throttle for top offenders. Who are top tenants? top-5: acme-inc, betaapp, genplay, queryly, internal-loadtest.

pm-lucy: flagged acme-inc is hitting 5x baseline due to a rollout. Reached out to their eng lead already (on email).

oncall-jordan: mitigation plan (live):
- step A: place emergency throttle on top-5 tenants (maya)
- step B: enable fallback routing for hosted-api to model variant redwood-3b-quant for non-SLA tenants (sina)
- step C: temporarily attach hosted traffic to dedicated-us-east-2 pool (ken + infra)
- step D: restart autoscaler controller after quota bump attempt (aj)
- step E: monitor queue and latencies, update customer success (pm-lucy)

maya: doing A now: /infra throttle set --tenants acme-inc,betaapp,genplay --rate 20r/s --reason "emergency throttle: usa-east queue surge"
maya: 👍 throttles in place, logs show inbound QPS for acme-inc down ~78% within 15s.

sina: starting B: flipping fallback routing flag for route: /v1/generate (hosted-api) -> fallback model redwood-3b-quant for plan != enterprise. Command:
```
redwood-cli route update --route /v1/generate --fallback-model redwood-3b-quant --scope non-enterprise
```

sina: fallback routing enabled. initial canary shows 30% of non-enterprise traffic hitting quant variant, latency p95 for those dropped to ~230ms.

ken: working on C - request to bind dedicated-us-east-2 pool to hosted routing. Need infra approval. Request submitted: infra MR #2419. If approved will take ~7-10m to reconfigure.

aj: we tried scaling autoscaler controller: saw error in controller logs: "error: cloudquota: request denied: compute.gpu.quotaExceeded". I've requested quota bump via cloud support but ETA unknown. I'll try restarting controller to clear stuck requests: `kubectl -n redwood-system rollout restart deployment/autoscaler-controller`

aj: restarted controller at 2136451325. watching logs.

incident-bot: NOTE: Incident severity bumped to SEV2 per playbook (latency p95>2s and widespread customer retries). Running pager cycle. @oncall-jordan assigned as IC.

oncall-jordan: assigning tasks: maya = tenant throttles & customer comms, sina = fallback routing + metrics, ken = dedicated pool bind, aj = autoscaler + infra, pm-lucy = CS notify + support tickets.

pm-lucy: notifying CS -> sent templated message to impacted accounts: acme-inc, betaapp, genplay, queryly. Provided mitigation ETA 15-30m.

maya: tenant throttles holding. Queue depth dropped from 11.2k -> 6.5k in 90s. Good trend.

sina: fallback routing ramped to 60% for non-enterprise. Non-enterprise p95 now 180-250ms. Hosted overall p95 down to 1.4s but p99 still spiky due to long running jobs.

ken: infra approved binding, started change at 2136451500. Cluster reconfig applying. Requesting temporary ACL change: `/infra bind-pool --from dedicated-us-east-2 --to hosted-us-east --duration 30m`

aj: autoscaler controller restart cleared backoff; it started issuing scale requests at 2136451560 but hit cloud quota denies again for 3 instances. However, because we bound dedicated pool, new nodes can be scheduled on borrowed GPUs. Pods are starting at 2136451620.

incident-bot: UPDATE: queue_depth falling. queued_requests=2300 at 2136451700.

oncall-jordan: good. Keep throttles until we have stable headroom. Maya leave throttles for 20m then gradual relax.

maya: leaving throttles at 20r/s for acme-inc, 10r/s for betaapp, others 15r/s. Will relax at 2136452600 if steady.

aj: autoscaler logs show a burst of successful scale ops after dedicated bind. We're adding ~8 GPU-backed pods. Pod images: hosted-runtime:v3.2.4.

sina: observations: major contributor to p99 were long-context encoder-heavy streams from genplay and internal-loadtest. We'll file followups to cap max-seq for non-enterprise.

pm-lucy: CS update: told customers we mitigated and are monitoring. Some customers reported transient 502/504 earlier; collecting exact error rates.

ken: pool bind will be released at 2136453300 (manual rollback planned) unless we extend. Recommend postmortem for dedicated borrow policy.

incident-bot: ACTIONS LOGGED: throttles applied, fallback routing toggled, dedicated pool bound, autoscaler restarted. Incident ID: INC-2026-2136451200.

oncall-jordan: monitoring 10m after mitigations: queued_requests 900, p95 420ms, p99 1.1s. We can start controlled rollback of emergency actions. Steps: 1) relax throttles by 50% -> maya, 2) reduce fallback to 30% -> sina, 3) keep dedicated bind until capacity stable -> ken, 4) keep autoscaler logs on debug for 1h -> aj.

maya: relaxing throttles now.

sina: reducing fallback to 30% now.

incident-bot: CUSTOMER IMPACT SUMMARY: acme-inc (elevated errors 502/504 12m window, best-effort routing to quant fallback), betaapp (rate-limited, degraded throughput), ~14 other tenants saw elevated latency. No known data loss.

pm-lucy: captured impacted accounts and opened CS tickets: CS-8851, CS-8852.

oncall-jordan: handoff notes for next oncall (assign to @ken):
- root cause: sudden traffic surge + cloud GPU quota exhaustion led autoscaler to fail creating new GPU nodes; response: emergency tenant throttles + fallback routing + bind dedicated pool.
- mitigation chronology & timestamps in incident doc: https://wiki.redwood/incidents/INC-2026-2136451200
- action items: (1) request permanent quota increase or autoscaler fallback path (2) add alert for autoscaler "quota_exceeded" and stuck backoff (3) add playbook entry to borrow dedicated pool and required approvals (4) investigate long-context tenant capping and routing to CPU fallback for non-SLA customers.

ken: taking handoff. I’ll keep pool bound for now and start runbook update.

oncall-jordan: thanks team. Marking page resolved at 2136452400. Will file postmortem with timeline + root cause + remediation by EOD.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: SEV2 -> resolved. Postmortem assigned to oncall-jordan.
